claims: KnowMe contains committed prometheus_entity_management and gen_ui_widgets package histories.
The active KnowMe worktree is dirty and must not be copied directly.
No root or package-local license is tracked for those Flutter packages.
The reusable package history begins in commit 2b1647ec9eb3914d6088a312b783fb651d3a8da4.
The repository is MIT licensed.
Its AGENTS.md and builder manifest identify it as a scaffolding/template skill, not a runnable application or canonical Flutter runtime library.
It is reference-only for this migration.
The destination release contract is MIT and declares entity_graph_flutter as the one stable Dart graph/Riverpod artifact.
Unlicensed Flutter source is a release blocker.
pub.dev publication is deferred and cannot be inferred from source import.
git-filter-repo supports extracting a directory and moving it under a destination subdirectory.
Filtering rewrites commit hashes and should run in a fresh disposable clone.
The commit-map provides an audit mapping between original and rewritten commits.
GitHub documents git-filter-repo path extraction for splitting subdirectory history.
The operation creates rewritten history and belongs in a separate clone.
REUSE 3.3 requires unambiguous copyright and license information for covered files.
SPDX identifiers and REUSE.toml can associate licensing information with imported paths.
License text must exist for each declared license.
A published Dart package includes a LICENSE file.
Package layout distinguishes public source, tests, examples, and tooling.
Riverpod 3 enables automatic provider retry by default.
AutoDispose interfaces and family notifier variants changed.
Terminal failures therefore require an explicit retry policy rather than an assumed 2.x behavior.
flutter_riverpod 3.4.2 is the latest and resolvable version observed by flutter pub outdated.
The destination currently resolves 2.6.1 while the KnowMe source pins 3.3.1.
The installed Flutter beta is 3.47.0-0.1.pre with Dart 3.13 beta.
The standalone Dart executable is 3.12.2 stable, so commands must record which toolchain resolved packages.
